g.text: Kinetic rocking module · NEMA 17 + TMC2209 + TinyPICO + BNO055 · redrawn from hand sketch IMG_3484
Symbol mirrored for routing: left column = board’s RIGHT header (BAT…25),
right column = board’s LEFT header (23…GND). Physical view on sheet 2.
Confirm coil pairing with a meter before power-up: 2–4 Ω between the two wires of one
coil, open circuit across coils. Mis-paired A/B gives buzz and no rotation.
Add C1, 100 µF / ≥25 V low-ESR, across VM–GND within 20 mm of U1. Without it the coil
inductive kick can exceed the TMC2209’s 29 V absolute max. Commonest cause of dead drivers.
Add R1, 10 kΩ from EN to +3V3. EN is active-low and ESP32 pins float through boot, so
without it the coils can energise before firmware runs — a real hazard on a fleet.
Optional: PDN_UART → IO4 through 1 kΩ. Enables UART mode — run/hold current, microstep,
StealthChop and StallGuard all set in firmware. Worth one wire for per-unit calibration.
MS1/MS2 open reads as 1/8 microstep with 256-step interpolation on most StepSticks.
Break them out to jumpers or IO14/IO15 if you want 1/16 or 1/32 in hardware.
The second “PDN” in the sketch is vendor-dependent — usually DIAG or INDEX.
Read the silkscreen before locking the footprint pin map.
U3 VIN on +3V3: breakout LDOs drop ~0.3 V, so the sensor rail lands near 3.0 V. It runs,
but if USB is always present prefer VIN → 5V. Check your module’s regulator.
VM = 10 V is legal (4.75–29 V) but caps step rate at a given torque. 12–24 V gives much
more headroom for fast wobble transitions. Size the supply for ≥ 1.2 × 2 × I_run.
Set the VREF trimpot before the first motion test. Factory position is usually far too hot
for a NEMA 17 on a 10 V rail, and a hot driver changes your motion model between units.
U3’s magnetometer will be corrupted by M1’s field and the coil traces. Run BNO055 in
IMUPLUS mode (accel + gyro) and place U3 as far from M1 and the VM loop as the board allows.
